This downward pressure becomes even more pronounced when considers the possibility of insurance--most people don't pay for ER visits on-site, but pay monthly premiums to an insurance company, which then pays the care center on their behalf. Because consumer demand is much more elastic between insurance policies, and insurance firm demand for care centers is more elastic than individual demand for care centers (on account of it being an ongoing cost across multiple clients for an insurance firm). All of these factors working in concert cause the price for emergency care to remain comparatively low in an unrestricted market.
